nodes.label: SponsorX Implementation Guide V2
nodes.rationale: Phase 1 engineering handoff: repo layout, the Prisma schema and the load-bearing patterns — tenant scoping, transactional job enqueue, the two tracking funnels, Zoho loop prevention, signature capture, authorization test matrix. Supersedes V1 (written against Vercel + Neon); aligned to .claude/stack-decision.md including Addendum A.

nodes.label: V2 Prisma Schema
nodes.rationale: Four conventions through every model: tenantId on everything, state enums lifted verbatim from §21, external IDs plus sync-origin marker on anything Zoho touches, events stored as rows not counters. V2 adds Property, Guardian, CampaignBrief, SponsorPackage, AthleteScore, WebhookDelivery over V1's core tables.

nodes.label: Tenant Scoping Pattern (actor.ts / scope.ts)
nodes.rationale: actor.ts answers who is asking, scope.ts answers what they may see; roles live on the Postgres User row, not in Clerk — authorization stays in tables we control per Addendum A4.

nodes.label: Two Tracking Funnels (RewardEvent vs TrackingLink)
nodes.rationale: V1 bug: tracking-link scans were written to RewardEvent.tokenId, which foreign-keys RewardToken — a TrackingLink id there fails the constraint. V2 fixes it as two funnels, two models.

nodes.label: Transactional Outbox + pg-boss
nodes.rationale: outbox.ts provides transactional enqueue; the worker boots pg-boss (queues live in our Postgres, migrations run on worker boot) and drains the outbox — so a domain write and its side-effect job commit atomically.

nodes.label: Authorization Test Matrix (authz.matrix.test.ts)
nodes.rationale: §30 makes cross-tenant and role authorization tests an acceptance criterion; the vitest matrix in tests/ makes those real tests against our own tables.

nodes.label: Repo Layout — One Repo, Two Deployables
nodes.rationale: Next app + worker as two services in one Railway project over private networking, both importing src/server so a job and a route handler can never disagree. Not a monorepo: two package.json files would mean two lockfiles drifting apart on the code that decides how much an athlete gets paid. Contracts are Zod schemas in src/contracts feeding OpenAPI generation.

nodes.label: R2 Two-Bucket Presign Pattern
nodes.rationale: Presigned PUT/GET via @aws-sdk against two buckets (public CDN vs private signed) plus image derivatives on the worker without next/image — implementing Addendum A8 while staying host-portable.
